title: Claude Code Masks Your Credentials From Its Own Sandbox
caption:
My GitHub token was sitting in the environment of every sandboxed command Claude ran, and I never once thought about it.

Claude Code's sandbox can mask it instead. The command reads a fake per-session sentinel, and the proxy swaps in the real token on the way out to api.github.com. gh still works. Nothing the command logs holds the secret.

The part that sold me: a repo's .claude/settings.json can't turn masking on. Only your user settings or your admin's can. So cloning someone else's project can't talk your proxy into injecting your keys somewhere.

Where do your keys live right now?

slides.headline:
Your agent authenticates.
Never sees the key.
slides.sub: Claude Code's sandbox hands commands a fake per-session sentinel. The proxy swaps in the real credential on the way out.

slides.title:
Sentinel in,
real key out
items: Set mode: mask on an env var. The sandboxed command reads a per-session sentinel, never the real value.
On egress the sandbox proxy substitutes the real credential, only for the hosts you list in injectHosts.
The command, and anything it logs, never holds the secret. Its requests still authenticate.

slides.headline:
deny breaks gh
and npm
slides.sub: deny unsets the variable entirely, so tools that need it stop working. mask keeps them working with the real token outside the sandbox.

slides.headline:
Repos can't
enable it
slides.sub: mask entries, network.tlsTerminate and awsPairs are honored only from user settings, managed settings, or --settings. A repo's .claude/settings.json is ignored.

slides.title:
Files, not just
env vars
items: mode: mask works on files. An extract regex masks only capture group 1, so gh still parses hosts.yml.
decode: jwt swaps in a structurally valid fake token, so code that decodes it keeps working.
Linux and WSL2 read a sentinel copy. On macOS the file is blocked instead.

slides.title: Three sharp edges
items: Masking needs network.tlsTerminate. Without it the sentinel reaches the server and auth fails, but nothing leaks.
For AWS, mask the access key and the secret together. The proxy spots SigV4 by the sentinel and re-signs.
Directories, globs, files over 8 MiB and non-UTF-8 files fall back to deny.

slides.headline:
Keys out of
the sandbox
slides.sub: and I'll send my sandbox settings
